note_claims.claim: The patient is presenting with dysuria and urinary frequency for one day.
The patient has experienced dysuria and frequency (about every 30 minutes) since Saturday.
The patient reported possible pink-tinged urine this morning.
The patient denies loin pain, fever, rigors, nausea, or vomiting.
The patient denies vaginal discharge or itching.
The patient has a history of one previous UTI two years ago, treated with antibiotics (agent unknown).
The patient's period is approximately one week late.
The patient has not yet had a pregnancy test.
The patient has no known renal disease.
The patient takes Vitamin D in the winter.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The abdomen is soft.
The patient has mild suprapubic tenderness.
The patient has no renal angle tenderness.
The patient is speaking in full sentences and sounds well.
The impression is a lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).
Possible early pregnancy is noted and needs to be excluded.
The treatment plan is to prescribe nitrofurantoin 100 mg modified-release capsules twice daily for seven days.
A pregnancy test is required today.
A urine sample is required for culture before starting antibiotics.
No routine follow-up is needed.
The patient should drink plenty of fluids and take paracetamol for discomfort.
The patient should avoid ibuprofen until pregnancy is excluded.
The patient should call the practice or 111 immediately if they develop pain in their back or side, a fever, shivering, or vomiting.
The patient should call back if they do not start to feel better within 48 hours of starting antibiotics or if they get worse.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician is Dr Whitlock calling back from the surgery.
Patient's date of birth is the second of November, ninety-seven.
Patient reports burning when urinating (dysuria) and needing to go every half an hour (frequency).
Duration of symptoms is three days (since Saturday).
Patient reports maybe a little pinkish urine this morning.
Patient denies pain in the back or sides, just under the ribs.
Patient denies fever, shivers, or shakes.
Patient denies feeling sick or vomiting.
Patient denies unusual vaginal discharge or itching.
Patient had a previous UTI about two years ago, which cleared up after antibiotics.
Patient's period is about a week late.
Patient takes Vitamin D in the winter.
Patient denies any drug allergies.
Patient denies problems with kidneys.
Clinician suggests the condition sounds like a urine infection in the bladder (cystitis).
Clinician plans to prescribe nitrofurantoin 100 milligrams, modified-release capsules, twice a day for seven days.
Clinician requests the patient do a pregnancy test today and drop a urine sample before starting antibiotics.
Clinician requests the patient ring back tomorrow with the pregnancy test result.
Clinician advises the patient to drink plenty of fluids and take paracetamol for discomfort.
Clinician advises sticking to paracetamol for now until pregnancy status is known.
Clinician advises calling straight away or 111 if the patient develops pain in the back or side, a fever, shivering, or vomiting.
Clinician advises calling back if the patient is not starting to feel better within 48 hours of starting antibiotics or if they are getting worse.
